title: The Last Piece
subject: a man who hides the final piece of his partner's thousand-piece jigsaw in his pocket so they can finish it together on a Sunday night
caption: UK neo-soul pop in the 2025 London jazz-soul singer-songwriter style. Brushed drums with a soft rim click; a round upright bass; a nylon-string guitar picking light chords; a jazz piano voicing major-seventh and ninth chords; a soft flugelhorn answering the voice between lines. Intimate and natural production, little reverb, audible room tone, piano and voice centred. Female alto, warm and close-miked, phrasing a little behind the beat, light self-harmony in the chorus. 84 BPM, D major. Tender, unhurried and quietly happy. No trap drums, no autotune, no big pop drop, no synth pads, no gospel choir.
lyrics:
[Intro - jazz piano and brushed snare]

[Verse 1]
Three weeks of sky on the coffee table
All of it blue and you sorted every shade
Edges done the first night like you always do
You hum when you find one, you don't know you do

[Pre-Chorus]
Nine hundred ninety-nine
And one in my jeans

[Chorus]
Leave the last piece for me
It's a lighthouse window, it's the size of my thumb
Leave the last piece for me
I want to be there when it's done

[Verse 2]
You searched the carpet, you lifted the cat
You swore at the box and the lighthouse on the lid
I came in with tea and I put down a mug
And I pulled out my hand and you knew, and you laughed

[Pre-Chorus]
You said you are the worst
Then you made room on the couch

[Chorus]
Put the last piece in with me
Your hand on my hand, push it in by the frame
Put the last piece in with me
Then tip out the next one again

[Outro - piano and flugelhorn]
Two thousand pieces next time
Leave the corner for me
